Start from the best-matching template above if one fits the request. SLIDE FRAME CONSTRAINTS: - Every slide renders into a FIXED 1280x720px frame (16:9). The frame never grows to fit content. - Size each slide's root element to exactly 1280 by 720 pixels and make it clip its own overflow — do not rely on any particular class name or wrapper structure; whatever the slide's outermost element is, anything past its frame must be CLIPPED on export, never scrolled. - One slide per frame: fit ALL of that slide's content inside its single 1280x720 frame, with no in-slide scrolling. Styling the root like a floating print-preview card shifts everything past the frame edge, and the bottom of the slide gets clipped on every surface and in every export. - Decorative imagery (cover art, corner motifs, background illustrations) must never overlap text content: keep titles, subtitles, list items, and footers fully clear of any artwork layer. resolved_data.synthesis: Structured prompting beats ad-hoc prompting on token cost, output consistency and the number of revision rounds needed to reach production quality.

figures.value: 30–50% fewer tokens per request vs. naive prompts
up to 40% output consistency gain with few-shot + chain-of-thought
3–5 revision rounds to reach production-grade quality

html:
The Problem

Ad-hoc prompting silently drains budget, quality, and velocity

Three compounding costs most teams overlook

  • Inconsistent outputs — Without structured prompts, the same query yields wildly different results, forcing manual review and rework every time
  • Wasted tokens & inflated cost — Naive prompts consume 30–50% more tokens than structured alternatives, a gap that scales with every API call
  • Slow iteration cycles — Teams typically need 3–5 revision rounds to reach production-grade quality, burning engineering hours on trial and error
Every unoptimised prompt is a recurring tax — on spend, on consistency, and on time-to-value. These costs compound with every new use case you ship.
Source: Industry benchmarks (OpenAI, Anthropic best-practice guides)1
